newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weaker yen boosts Yamaha's motorcycle profits.
newsitem.headline: Weaker yen boosts Yamaha's motorcycle profits.

text.p: Yamaha Motor Co Ltd, the world's second-biggest motorcycle maker, said on Wednesday that the weaker yen had boosted exports, translating into a 270 percent jump in half-year profits.

Other top motorcycle makers such as Honda Motor Co Ltd and Suzuki Motor also said exports for the fiscal year to the end of March would be higher than earlier predicted, but still down on figures from the year-ago period.
Yamaha said its parent current profit in the first half rose because of the weaker yen, cost-cutting and increased motorcycle sales abroad.

Yamaha's current profit in the half-year was 4.53 billion yen ($40.8 million), up 269.2 percent from a year ago. It revised up full-year forecast to 8.5 billion yen ($76.5 million) from a May prediction of 7.5 billion yen ($67.5 million), against 5.7 billion yen ($51.3 million) a year ago.
Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
"The weaker yen is a major part of the upward revisions in motorcycle exports this business year, making Japanese products more competitive on pricing," a Yamaha spokesman said.
Yamaha saved 11.1 billion yen ($100 million) because of the weaker yen in the first half after it lost 10.3 billion yen ($92.7 million) because of the stronger yen last year, he said.
The dollar is now trading at around 111 yen, recovering from about 80 yen at the start of the previous fiscal year in April 1995.
Yamaha raised its forecast for motorcycle exports to 410,000, up from a May forecast of 380,000 and up from 370,000 a year earlier.

Honda Motor Co Ltd, the world's top motorcycle maker, in August raised its forecast for full-year motorcycle exports to 460,000 from a previous forecast of 420,000, due to higher-than-expected demand in Asia. But that is still down from exports of 470,000 a year earlier.
Its forecast for domestic sales remained unchanged from a May forecast of 670,000, up from 641,000 a year earlier.
Honda's motorcycle division has helped sales and profit in the past when the company struggled with poor car sales.
Sales by the motorcycle division account for 14 percent of overall group sales. Honda will announce its half-year business results on Friday.

Suzuki Motor on Tuesday revised up its forecast for exports to 309,000 motorcycles from a May forecast of 281,000 due to higher-than-expected demand for its new sporty models in Europe, but down from 346,000 a year earlier.
Sales of Suzuki's motorcycle division accounted for 13.9 percent of total parent sales in the half-year.
Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd, which produces bigger models, estimated motorcycle exports of 186,000 in 1996/97, slightly more than the 184,000 the year before.
It also expects to export 355,000 knockdown kits, up from 251,000. Its domestic sales will fall to 38,000 this year from 41,000, a spokesman said. ($1=111 yen)
